overall: The AG found the Selectboard violated the OML by not announcing recording at five May–June 2025 meetings, but found the automated Teams recording pop-up for remote attendees lawful.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Selectboard failed to announce at the start of its May 20, May 22, May 29, June 3, and June 5 meetings that they were being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: The Board does not dispute that no announcement of recording was made at the start of the Board’s May 20, May 22, May 29, June 3, and June 5 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged remote attendees joining via Microsoft Teams were forced to see a pop-up stating they would be recorded, which it said was a separate violation.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent this point is intended as a separate alleged violation of the Open Meeting Law, we find that the automated notification, which is built into the Teams platform, does not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements to announce any recording of open sessions at the start of the meeting.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
